item.title: Safety hazard regarding a temporary, modular plastic speed restriction ramp, 29th September
item.description:
I was cycling this section of New Kent Road at night and hit this modular plastic speed ramp at full pace on a Lime bike. The area wasn’t adequately lit and I didn’t see any ramp warning signs. I was thrown from the bike and sustained cuts and bruises over my arms, legs, hands and feet. A quick check of highway codes suggests that these types of temporary cable covering ramps are intended for private property or off-street commercial yards - they are not to be used on major London dual carriageways. At night this lane is open (there’s no red tape across the road). Cars come down the right hand side so as a cyclist the tendency is funnel into the bus lane rather than squeeze down the concrete partition to the right. The off-street style plastic modular ramp is a hazard to cyclists but also emergency services. Please can you investigate to prevent others from hurting themselves?

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 197-209, New Kent Road, Walworth, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
